subject: What to pass to ggplot when column name is not yet known?

messages.author: 4114912dbf9e2d36
messages.subject: What to pass to ggplot when column name is not yet known?
parts:
I am using shiny and ggplot where I ask the user to select a column, and plot a histogram. I understand that ggplot takes the name the column as one of the inputs, but I don't know which column the user will select. for example:
x  <- WhatDoISetThisTo
qplot(x, data = myDataFrame)

I have tired:
x <- "name"
qplot(x, data = myDataFrame)

But this doesn't work as x is now a string and not the column name. I have also tried:
x <- "name"
qplot(myDataFrame[,x], data = myDataFrame)

But this gives me an error telling me the rows number don't match. This confuses me as I know the row the numbers are the same. So how should I set x to pass to ggplot?

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: What to pass to ggplot when column name is not yet known?
parts:
I would suggest you use ggplot() over qplot(). You can use `aes_string()` to pass on variables (of strings).

Cheers,
Roman
